steps.prompt: An agent has two topics, Order Cancellation and Subscription Billing. Customers asking to "stop my monthly box", "cancel auto-ship", or "end recurring shipments" are routed to Order Cancellation, whose actions can only cancel one-off orders. How should the architect fix the routing?

options.label: Rewrite both topic descriptions to state what each covers and which requests it excludes
options.rationale: The agent chooses a topic by matching the request against each topic’s description and scope, so overlapping descriptions misroute requests whatever the actions can do. Drawing the one-off versus recurring boundary there works for every way customers phrase a subscription.

options.label: Merge both topics into one topic that holds all the cancellation and billing actions
options.rationale: Merging moves the same ambiguity into action selection: the agent must still tell a one-off cancellation from a subscription stop, now among the actions of two domains.

options.label: Add a rule that routes messages containing "recurring" or "subscription" to Subscription Billing
options.rationale: Customers already say "monthly box" and "auto-ship", so a keyword list misses every phrasing it does not name and needs endless upkeep.

options.label: Add an Order Cancellation instruction to hand subscription requests to Subscription Billing
options.rationale: Topic instructions apply only after the topic is chosen, so every subscription request still lands in Order Cancellation first and relies on the LLM to notice the mistake.
